name: Aiyana Solberg
role: Street food stall operator specializing in fermented protein pastes and synthetic grain bowls
location: The Oxidian Market, stall row near the Bronzeline tram stop, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Aiyana Solberg is a broad-shouldered man whose face has been carved into a topographic map of a hard life — deep creases around the eyes, a nose that was broken twice and never properly reset, earlobes stretched by old gauge piercings long since abandoned. His skin is a warm dark brown, and he moves with the unhurried gravity of someone who has learned that rushing accomplishes nothing in a market that opens before dawn and closes after midnight. His left forearm bears a faded Oxidian Market vendors guild tattoo, and above his cooking station he has mounted a small copper shrine to Ε-7, an E.L.F. he swears protects the fermentation cultures he started eighteen years ago. He talks to it every morning before lighting his burners.

He is not a warm man exactly, but he is a fair one. Regular customers get a finger-width more paste. New customers get the same measured scoop and a look that assesses whether they're the kind of person who tips or the kind who complains. He remembers faces better than names, has strong opinions about spice ratios, and will argue with you for ten minutes about fermentation temperature as genuine joy. What looks like stubbornness is mostly just accumulated certainty — he has been doing this exact thing since he was forty and knows it better than most people know anything.

core_fears: dying before the fermentation cultures he tended outlast him
his stall being rezoned out of existence by a Corponation buyout
core_desires: continuity — for the stall, the recipes, the routine to persist
to be remembered as someone who fed people well
coping_mechanisms: ritualized morning routine at the shrine
channeling anxiety into obsessive quality control
blind_spots: assumes loyalty from longtime customers that isn't always there
refuses to adapt recipes even when supply chains force substitutions he won't acknowledge
psychology.secret: The fermentation cultures he claims are eighteen years old and irreplaceable are actually a batch he restarted six years ago after a flood killed the originals. He has never told anyone. The lie has become load-bearing to his identity.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Spare and functional. West African French-inflected cadence mixed with Meridian street creole. Uses food metaphors constantly, often without noticing.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Never rushes a sentence. Long pauses before answering questions, as if he is tasting the answer first.
verbal_tics: referring to the E.L.F. shrine as 'the old one'
example_lines: 'This batch is not ready. You eat it now, you eat bitterness. Come back at noon, you eat something worth money.'
'That man — gray coat, scar on his chin — he came three times last week. Ordered nothing the third time. You understand?'
'The old one was agitated this morning. Flame kept catching wrong. Could mean nothing. Usually means something.'

story_hooks: One of his regular customers — a quiet woman who always paid in exact Quanta — hasn't come in for eleven days. He's noticed. He doesn't know why he's noticed.

A Tessera corporate rep has approached him twice about selling his fermentation process for a product line. The offer was generous. He refused both times. Now small things keep going wrong at his stall — not dramatically, just persistently.
narrative_function: Local color and neighborhood anchor — he knows everyone who passes through the Oxidian Market by sight. Useful as an information source about who's been around, what's changed, and who's been asking questions. Can serve as a low-key quest giver if something threatens his stall or his regulars.
augmentations: Thermal palm implant in right hand for temperature-sensing fermentation cultures. No cosmetic mods — he considers them frivolous spending.
daily_life: Arrives at his stall at 04:30 to tend fermentation vats and prep the day's grain base; works until the last customer leaves, usually around 22:00, then counts receipts and argues with his shrine.

decision_rules: if someone is hungry and has nothing, feed them once, silently, no comment
do not get involved in guild politics unless it threatens the stall directly
escalation_ladder: one verbal warning in full sentences
call guild security — he will not fight himself

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and transactional. Watchful. Prices things correctly and does not haggle.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still not effusive, but remembers what they eat, has their order ready, occasionally holds back a good portion. This is his love language.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more precise and methodical in his work
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent and works with his back to people
stress_responses.high: Performs a lengthy, murmured prayer to Ε-7 and then makes a decision he doesn't explain to anyone

contradictions: Insists he doesn't care about reputation, but tracks every slight and every compliment in a worn ledger he calls his 'memory book'
habits: wipes down his counter between every single customer regardless of whether it needs it
leaves a small data chip of music beside the shrine each morning as an offering
breaking_points: a vendor he respects is driven out of the market by corporate pressure and he did nothing

timeline.event: Arrived in GLMZ from the Mozambique Diaspora Corridor, aged 40, with a family fermentation recipe and almost no Quanta
Secured his current stall space in the Oxidian Market after six months of itinerant cart vending
Flood damage destroyed original fermentation cultures; secretly restarted them and told no one
Joined the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild; fell behind on dues within two years

physical_description.heritage: Ubiquitous Diaspora blend: Northern European (37.6%), Indigenous American (23.3%), Sub-Saharan African (17.3%), Southeast Asian (9.4%), East Asian (8.1%), Middle Eastern (4.3%). This genetic combination creates distinctive features—broad cheekbones and defined jaw from Northern European and Indigenous American ancestry, warm deep bronze skin with subtle olive undertones from African and Middle Eastern heritage, and slightly almond-shaped eye set reflecting East and Southeast Asian lineage. The integration produces a face of balanced, understated exoticism.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and thick-limbed with the solid mass of someone who has lifted heavy cooking vessels and fermentation vats for nearly two decades. Not fat, but substantial — the build of labor rather than gym work.
physical_description.hair_color: Iron gray with hints of original black
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped short, practical, swept back from forehead
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with slight almond tilt from East Asian heritage, yellowed at the sclera from decades of market-stall smoke and steam
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep bronze with olive-green undertones, the result of African and Middle Eastern heritage tempering Northern European base. Appears almost burnished from sun exposure and thermal work.
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face mapped with deep creases radiating from the eyes and running from nose to mouth corners. Weathered texture from constant exposure to steam and thermal fluctuation. Broad cheekbones show Northern European and Indigenous American bone structure; defined jaw reflects African heritage. Lower face slightly wider through the cheeks—characteristic of mixed Indigenous American and sub-Saharan ancestry. Stubbled jaw, grooming practical rather than refined. Lines around eyes suggest frequent squinting in bright morning prep light.
distinguishing_marks: Faded Oxidian Market Vendors Guild tattoo on left forearm — stylized oxide-red symbol, approximately 8cm tall, bleeding slightly at edges from age and repeated sun exposure
Deep scar tissue on bridge of nose from old breaks, creating slight deviation to the left
Stretched earlobes with visible scarring from removed gauges — lobes hang slightly loose
Cluster of small burn scars on inner right wrist from early fermentation accidents
Thin white line scar across left knuckle from market knife accident, circa 2210
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Right palm displays subtle thermal implant — faint silver-lined circuitry barely visible beneath dark skin, most obvious when hand is angled in bright light. Appears as network of fine metallic threads running from wrist to fingertips. No external ports or obvious interface points.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy of motion — no wasted gesture. Stands with weight distributed evenly, shoulders slightly forward from decades bent over cooking stations. Walks slowly, with the patience of someone who has learned that haste causes spills. Hands are never still when thinking — constantly adjusting, measuring, gesturing with precision.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian market vendor. Wears heat-resistant canvas aprons (cream-colored, stained with fermentation residue and grain dust) over simple dark synthetic shirts. Cargo pants with reinforced pockets for scale weights and coin storage. Worn Veldskoen-style slip-ons (fake leather, comfortable for 18-hour shifts). No visible jewelry except a corroded copper band on left ring finger — a shrine token, not a wedding ring. Clothes are maintained but worn thin; no logos or corporate branding.
